findings.problem: fs::read_to_string and println! are hidden I/O fused into a session-loading function that should separate shell (I/O) from core (parsing/domain construction). File I/O, logging, parsing, allocation, and domain construction are all fused.
findings.failure_mode: shell side-effects leak into core logic, making the function impossible to unit-test in isolation, breaking the Data/Calculations/Actions boundary, and making it impossible to swap I/O backends or mock file reads.
findings.fix: Split into shell: fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<String, IoError> and core: fn parse_sessions(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>. Move fs::read_to_string and println! into the shell layer only.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found, permission errors, or invalid UTF-8.
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file input aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error that the caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)) without unwrap.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input for the value field.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input (e.g. "bad,notanumber") aborts the entire session load instead of returning a typed parse error for the specific offending row.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Invalid(value_index))? to return a typed parse error instead of panicking.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked index access on a split result. If a line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, this panics with an index-out-of-bounds panic.
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed line (e.g., "onlyonename") causes a panic rather than a typed parse error, violating panic freedom and failing to isolate bad rows.
findings.fix: Replace the entire parts-collection pattern with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::InvalidRow)? and bind (_name, value_str) = ...; use value_str for parsing. For two-field records, split_once avoids indexing, bounds checks, and get() entirely.

findings.problem: (parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16) is a lossy cast: any u32 value > 65535 silently truncates to u16 with no error.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 like 70000 silently becomes 4467 in the domain Record, corrupting data with no indication that the value exceeded the domain range.
findings.fix: Replace with u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)? using destination-type try_from instead of lossy as cast.

findings.problem: let parts: Vec<String> = line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a full intermediate Vec of owned Strings for every line, when only two fields are needed.
findings.failure_mode: Wasted allocation per line increases memory pressure and allocation overhead. For large session files this is unnecessary and contradicts the 'avoid intermediate Vec/String materialization unless required' principle. Also enables unchecked indexing instead of structured parsing.
findings.fix: Eliminate the parts vector. Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to destructure directly, parse value_str, and construct Record without intermediate allocation.

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no bounded capacity, no domain cap, no try_reserve, and no maximum session count validation.
findings.failure_mode: An unbounded file (e.g., millions of lines) can allocate unbounded memory, leading to OOM kill or denial of service with no allocation budget or domain cap enforcement.
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap/max_rows first, collect into Vec::new(), then use values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before pushes. Reject empty input early. Add max_rows parameter or domain constant.

findings.problem: Function signature returns Vec<Record> with no Result type. All errors (I/O, parse, overflow, allocation, malformed input) are silently converted to panics via unwrap().
findings.failure_mode: Callers have no way to distinguish a missing file from a malformed CSV row from an integer overflow. Error handling is impossible at the API level.
findings.fix: Define a typed error enum: enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), InvalidRow, Parse(u32), Overflow(u32), Allocation }; change signature to fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>.
